absent: Full memory layouts, field offsets and sizes for held locks, graph nodes, classes and traces.
Numeric values and bit positions for usage, direction, state and read masks and lock flavor enumerations.
Implementation of breadth first traversal, root setup, parent and depth helpers and stack-trace capture.
Contracts of printing helpers, kernel identity output, held-lock dumps and the class comparison hook.
Graph mutation and locking protocol outside the counting queries and any boot, ring, capability, rollback or lane interactions.
Exact log formatting, numeric return conventions for omitted helpers and thresholds for queue sizing.

findings.text: Provides a query that returns how many distinct dependency nodes are reachable forward from a given lock class. Callers supply the class of interest and receive a numeric tally.
Provides a query that returns how many distinct dependency nodes are reachable backward toward a given lock class. Callers supply the class of interest and receive a numeric tally.
Both directional tally queries preserve local interrupt state and hold the internal dependency guard while traversing, releasing the guard and restoring interrupt state before returning.

Internal directional tallies start from zero and delegate traversal to the corresponding breadth first walk with a visitor that increments the tally for every visited node and never requests early termination.

Circular-path matching succeeds only when the held item and the graph node share the same class, and additionally requires either that the held item is exclusive or that the graph edge is not marked as exclusive-read-only.

Backward usage collection merges the usage information of each visited class into a shared accumulator, but when the edge carries the exclusive-read-only marker only the interrupt-related portion is merged.

Forward and backward usage lookup reports a hit when the visited class usage overlaps the sought mask, again restricting the comparison to the interrupt-related portion for edges marked exclusive-read-only.

The irq-inversion traversal retains ordinary locks, retains per-CPU locks only when an inner wait-type sanity check triggers, and skips remaining special lock flavors so they do not contribute dependencies.
An alternate configuration disables interrupt-usage validation entirely by reporting success unconditionally and disables traversal skipping by never skipping any node.

Path validation delegates to a forward breadth first search from a supplied root toward a target, emits a traversal-error diagnostic if the walk reports an error, and returns the walk outcome to the caller.

The cycle validator maintains a diagnostic attempt counter and treats absence of a conflicting forward path as success. When such a path exists it guarantees a stack capture is available and selects recursive reporting for identical class indices versus circular reporting for distinct classes.

Two callable search entries expose forward and backward usage lookup from a caller-supplied root for a caller-supplied usage mask, returning the traversal outcome and optionally the matching node. Each direction maintains its own diagnostic attempt counter.

Traversal failures are surfaced through a dedicated diagnostic that distinguishes queue exhaustion, where it advises enlarging LOCKDEP_CIRCULAR_QUEUE_BITS, from other corruption-like errors reported with a numeric code.

The circular-dependency header is suppressed in silent mode. Otherwise it emits a banner with kernel identity, the current task identity, details of the lock being acquired and the lock already held, an explanation of the dependency direction, and the reverse-order chain.

Circular diagnosis captures a stack trace and aborts quietly if capture fails. Otherwise it emits the header, walks parent links toward the root emitting each link, then shows an illustrative interleaving, a held-lock summary and a backtrace within an emergency console section.

The circular illustration conditionally summarizes a three-node chain when the intermediate node differs from the source class, then presents a two-CPU interleaving that distinguishes read, exclusive and synchronization acquisition flavors and ends with a deadlock notice.

Recursive-lock reporting is suppressed in silent mode or when the debug-locks guard cannot be taken. Otherwise it emits a banner with task and lock details, optionally shows the outcome of the class comparison hook, then presents a single-CPU double-acquisition illustration with a nesting-notation hint, a held-lock summary and a backtrace.

The interrupt-safety illustration conditionally summarizes a three-node chain when the middle class differs from the unsafe endpoint, then presents a two-CPU scenario with interrupt disable, nested acquisition on one side and interrupt-time acquisition on the other, ending with a deadlock notice.

Unsafe ordering diagnosis emits a warning identifying the interrupt class, the task with hard and soft interrupt context counters and enable states, the new dependency edge, the safe endpoint with its activation trace and the unsafe endpoint with its activation trace, followed by an illustrative scenario, held-lock summary, shortest-path details in both directions and a backtrace.

Shortest-path printers start from a leaf and follow parent links toward the supplied root while tracking depth, emitting per-node class information and acquisition traces, with the backward variant delaying trace display by one node. If depth is exhausted away from the expected root they emit a malformed-path diagnostic.

Class detail shows the class name indented by depth, its accumulated operation tally when detailed debugging is enabled, each active usage state name with its activation trace, and the key identity with symbolic form. The tally is computed by summing per-CPU counters indexed by class offset.

Mask derivation preserves state while toggling direction between enabled and in-use portions, and expands between plain and read-extended forms so that exclusive and original counterparts can be compared across interrupt flavors.

Exclusive-pair search scans set bits of one mask for a counterpart whose flipped-direction form, or its read-extended form, appears in the other mask. Human-readable state naming selects the read table when the read marker is set and the plain table otherwise.

Interrupt-usage validation treats absence of backward interrupt usage, absence of a forward exclusive counterpart, or traversal errors as success after any required diagnostic. Only when both a backward safe lock and a forward unsafe lock are located and narrowed to an incompatible bit pair does it report failure.

Observed associations treat a held item as carrying a class reference, read and synchronization markers, an instance reference and a class index. A graph node carries a class reference, a trace reference, an exclusive-read-only marker and parent linkage. A class carries usage state, activation traces, a key, type and inner wait attributes and an optional comparison hook.

The fragments govern behavior through families of symbolic constants for interrupt usage masks, direction and state portions, read extensions, lock flavors and wait thresholds, traversal outcomes, queue sizing and trace-state counts.

Bug reporters first attempt to disable debug locks with graph release and return early when that fails or silent mode is set. On success they bracket all output within an emergency console section that is always released.

Reporting can be silently suppressed by global silent mode, can abort without output when stack-trace capture fails, and can emit a malformed-path diagnostic when parent-chain depth does not align with the expected root.
